title: Make backtest evidence postdate decisions and validate each citation
summary: Redo job 9gwv. The backtest dates a decision from the first commit that introduced its '## D87 ' id heading. It counts only later records, derives a merge refusal only when the HTTP code is tied to the refused merge, and fails on any invalid citation. Tests use fixture records with the exact kn3q, qk2d and ar1x text and times, and must show D87 under review citing only ar1x.

defaults_applied.how: Fixture-based tests for each fix; fmt, clippy and test must pass.
Fix the derivation tie, the start-time lookup and the citation validation, not only the D87 instance.
Behavior criteria run with cargo test, since the verifier has no records/.
Fixture text is the public intervention text, with no personal data.
The change stays inside the watcher and backtest modules and their tests.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The previous attempt's code is not in this copy: backtest.rs has no start_from_history, so the work is redone in full from the current tree.
With no records/ directory, the real-records run is not a criterion. The fixtures stand in for it.
The decision start comes from git log in the real repo. Tests inject a start time so they do not depend on history.

acceptance_criteria.text: A backtest test builds fixture records with the verbatim text and timestamps of kn3q (2026-10-13T15:07:02Z), qk2d (16:20:49Z) and ar1x (19:21:56Z), with D87 starting 2026-10-13T19:21Z. D87 is under review citing only ar1x, directly and through its derived record. kn3q and qk2d are not cited. Run: cargo test.

Unit tests: 'GitHub refused a merge commit (HTTP 405)' and 'Operator squash-merged PR #41 by hand ... after GitHub refused a merge commit (HTTP 405).' derive a merge refusal. kn3q's text derives nothing. 'I merged by hand because the push failed with HTTP 422' and 'the push failed with HTTP 422' derive nothing. Run: cargo test.
The refusal derivation requires the HTTP code to be tied to the refusal of the merge itself, for example 'refused a merge ... (HTTP 405)'. A bare 'merged' elsewhere in the text is not enough.

A decision's start time comes from the first commit that introduced its id heading ('## D87 '), not from its current full heading text. The code finds that commit with git history, and a test or code path shows that a renamed heading still dates from the first commit.

The backtest counts only records after the decision's start. It validates each cited record against the signal's fields and time window, and fails when any citation is invalid. A test with a pre-start cited record fails the backtest. Run: cargo test.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo test pass.
The clause splitting no longer breaks on decimal points or version numbers, or the derivation does not depend on it.

out_of_scope: Running the backtest over the real records
New signals or decisions beyond D87
departures: The change is larger than the reference: the prior attempt's code is absent, so this redoes the full job plus fixture tests. Cost and time are raised.
